description: Legacy baselines for the COBOL-vs-FastAPI parity harness (KAN-103). Every entry records how the data was obtained: 'mainframe-extract' baselines come from a real legacy run and can be signed off as a benchmark, 'derived-from-source-spec' baselines were written from the copybooks and program source and only prove the port matches the specification as read.

baselines.name: transactions_input
baselines.inputs: n/a - this file is the batch input the other baselines are produced from
baselines.notes: Five pending transactions on 2024-03-20 for PORT0001 and PORT0002. Sequence 000004 uses price 1234.5678 so the amount exercises truncation to the S9(13)V9(2) picture (10 x 1234.5678 = 12345.678 -> 12345.67); sequence 000005 is the only sale.

baselines.name: closing_prices
baselines.inputs: n/a - valuation input for the batch run
baselines.notes: Closing prices the market value in positions_after_batch is computed from. Fixed so the baseline is deterministic.

baselines.name: positions_after_batch
baselines.notes: Cost basis of a purchase is the sum of the transaction amounts, each already truncated to two decimals. The sale of 30 of 150 units of SEC0000001 removes cost at average cost (19062.50 x 30 / 150 = 3812.50 exactly, so the rule is unambiguous for this data set) and market value is quantity x closing price truncated to two decimals - neither rule is stated in the batch source, whose arithmetic paragraphs are not present, so both need confirmation before this file counts as a benchmark.

baselines.name: inqport_responses
baselines.inputs: positions_after_batch loaded into POSFILE; INQCOM-ACCOUNT-NO as given per request
baselines.notes: INQPORT does a single keyed READ of POSFILE and returns one position, so the response carries the POSREC fields at their copybook precision. The not-found case returns the literal 'Position not found for account' and leaves INQCOM-RESPONSE-CODE untouched - only P999-ERROR-ROUTINE sets it - which is why response_code is 0 there. INQPORT keys POSFILE by account number while POSREC is keyed by portfolio id; the account-to-portfolio mapping the port needs is not in the legacy source.

baselines.name: inqhist_responses
baselines.inputs: transactions_input loaded into POSHIST; account 1000000001, 2024-03-20 to 2024-03-20, page 1
baselines.notes: WS-HISTORY-TABLE holds ten rows ordered by TRANS_DATE descending, and its units and price are PIC S9(9)V99 - two decimals, against four in TRNREC - so the baseline rounds units and price to two decimals on purpose. The legacy cursor filters on account only, has no date predicate, and WS-MORE-HISTORY is never set, so the date range and paging in the modern endpoint have no legacy counterpart to compare against.
